notes.panic-exit-devices: A bar across the inside face of the door that unlatches under pressure, so a person leaving in a crowd needs no handle, no key and no instruction.
notes.night-latches-rim-locks: Mounted on the face of the door rather than inside it. Latches behind you on closing, and can be held open when a door needs to stay free.
notes.stainless-steel-handles: Pull and door handles in stainless steel, for entrances and glass doors where the handle is the visible hardware.
notes.lever-handles: Handles on roses or backplates, fitted to a lock case bought separately. A lever can be opened with an elbow or a closed fist, which a knob cannot.
notes.knob-locks: Lock and handle in one assembly, bored straight through the door face. The commonest lock on an interior door because it needs two holes and no chiselling.
notes.bathroom-accessories: Grab rails, hooks, holders and shelves — the fittings a washroom needs beyond its door.
notes.care-grab-bars: Grab bars for an accessible WC or bathroom — the support a user pulls against to transfer, sit or stand.
notes.brass-steel-hinges: Carries the door's weight and its whole life of movement. The item most often under-specified, and the one that fails first when it is.
notes.deadbolts: A bolt thrown by key or thumbturn with no spring behind it, so it cannot be pushed back. Fitted above a latch, not instead of one.
notes.door-closers: Controls the door's swing and closes it every time. Needed wherever a door must not be left standing open.
notes.grip-handle-sets: A long pull on the outside with a lock behind it, for a main entrance door.
notes.glass-door-accessories: Patch fittings, clamps and locks that grip toughened glass without a frame, holding the leaf at its corners.
notes.hardware-accessories: Strikes, spindles, screws, stops and the parts that make the rest fit.
notes.lock-cases: The mechanism itself, let into a pocket cut in the edge of the door. Handles and cylinders are ordered separately and fit to it.
notes.lock-cylinders: The keyed part. Changing the cylinder rekeys the door without touching the lock case.
notes.sliding-hook-locks: For a sliding leaf, where a bolt cannot travel straight out. A hook swings from the case into the keep.
notes.floor-springs-and-pivots: Pivot hardware: the door hangs on a spindle top and bottom rather than on hinges, and the floor spring both carries it and closes it.
notes.exterior-trim: The outside handle for a panic device: the escape bar works from inside regardless, and this decides whether the door can also be opened from outside.
notes.fire-door: Devices for openings that must hold a fire back and still let people out.
notes.special-applications: Devices for openings the standard patterns do not cover.
notes.multi-point: Throws several bolts up and down the leaf from one turn, pulling a tall door tight.
notes.alarmed: Sounds when the bar is pushed, for a door that is a legal exit but not a normal one.
notes.tubular-locks: Latch and spindle in a slim tube. Lighter duty than cylindrical, and quicker to fit.
notes.light-duty-cylindrical-locks: The same pattern, built for a residential opening rather than a corridor in constant use.
notes.heavy-duty-cylindrical-locks: A chassis inside the door with the working parts around the spindle. The pattern used in schools, hospitals and offices, where one door is opened thousands of times a year.
notes.commercial-locks: Cylindrical locks in the function sets a commercial specification asks for — classroom, storeroom, entrance, passage.
notes.fixed-grab-bars: A grab bar bolted to the wall and staying there — straight or L-shaped, sized to the reach between the pan and the wall.
notes.flip-up-grab-bars: A grab bar beside the WC that folds up flat to the wall. Down, it carries the transfer; up, it clears the space a wheelchair needs to come alongside — which is why an accessible plan draws it separately from a fixed bar.
notes.glass-door-handles: Pulls fixed through drilled toughened glass, with no frame to fix to.
notes.glass-door-patch-fittings: Corner castings that clamp toughened glass and carry the pivot, lock or rail.
notes.indicators: Shows occupied or vacant from outside, for a cubicle or a washroom.
notes.latches: The sprung bolt that holds a door closed without locking it.
notes.door-stoppers: Stops the leaf, and the handle on it, before either reaches the wall.
notes.door-viewers: A wide-angle lens through the door leaf, so the person inside can see the caller without opening.
notes.power-transfer-devices: Carries current from frame to leaf, so an electrified lock keeps working as the door swings.
notes.security-door-guards: Lets the door open a few centimeters on a restrictor, so a caller can be spoken to before being let in.
notes.door-flush-bolts: Holds the inactive leaf of a pair shut, let in flush so nothing stands proud of the edge.
notes.armoured-lock-covers: A steel plate over the latch on the outside of the door, so the gap cannot be worked open with a pry bar.
notes.house-numbers: Numerals and letters for the outside of the building.
notes.floor-springs: Concealed in the floor, carrying the door's whole weight and closing it — the door swings on the spindle, not on hinges.
notes.pivot-top-patches: Clamps the top of a frameless glass leaf onto the pivot. Chosen to match the floor spring below it.
notes.top-pivots: The upper half of a pivot set: it locates the door, the floor spring carries it.
